ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and officers must be screened before incorporation against (i) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and SEMA schedules administered by Global Affairs Canada; (ii) UN Security Council sanctions given effect under the United Nations Act; (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List where USD wire rails are used; and (iv) FINTRAC politically exposed person constructs under PCMLTFA s 9.2 and FINTRAC Guidance on PEPs. Positive PEP or sanctions hits require enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, verification of source of funds, and ongoing transaction screening; negative news monitoring is repeated quarterly thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Government of Alberta, administered by Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction), online filing through the Corporate Access portal (bizPAR) and NUANS name search conducted through accredited Corporate Registry agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a corporate name must be in English or French and consist of a distinctive element, an optional descriptive element, and the legal element. For an Alberta unlimited liability corporation, the legal element must be 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'Unlimited Liability Company', or the abbreviation 'ULC'. Names use Latin-alphabet characters, permitted punctuation, and Arabic numerals; foreign-script names (e.g., Mandarin, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters and cannot form the statutory name unless they satisfy the transliteration rules of the applicable Business Corporations Regulation. All registry filings and index entries are recorded in English.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the NUANS name is rejected, the applicant may file a written Request for Review with the Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), through the Corporate Access portal, within 30 days of the rejection, setting out the grounds for review and attaching a fresh NUANS report and any authorization letters for sensitive tokens; the Registrar issues a written confirmation or a renewed rejection. If the name is again refused, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSA 2000, c J-3, or may proceed immediately under a numbered name (e.g., 12345678 Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation) and file a subsequent name change under ABCA s 21. A rejected name may be freely resubmitted after the 90-day reservation window has lapsed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this MedTech regulatory consulting class (ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541690): the ULC must maintain at all times a registered office and registered records office at a physical street address in Alberta (a post office box is not sufficient), but a serviced virtual office with mail handling and an Alberta-licensed registered agent satisfies the ABCA s 97 requirements and is accepted by the Corporate Registry and most financial institutions for this low-risk, non-licensed business. No provincial professional licence mandates a brick-and-mortar consulting premises for FDA 510(k) or CE Mark advisory work.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 5-10% annual probability and roughly 15% cumulative over three years, driven predominantly by Canada Revenue Agency audit and substance verification and by FINTRAC record-keeping inspections if the firm holds client funds; the Alberta Corporate Registry does not conduct routine unannounced site visits for low-risk service ULCs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (ABCA), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended – Part 1.1, s. 10.1 et seq. (Unlimited Liability Corporation regime), and the ABCA incorporation, articles, registered office, and records provisions (ss. 6–9, 101, 115–116).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Government of Alberta) – online Corporate Registry filing portal and authorized service providers.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta) filed with the Corporate Registry; Certificate of Incorporation issued upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or trust account requirement under the ABCA. The ULC may incorporate with zero or nominal issued capital; the founding shareholder typically subscribes one or more no-par-value common shares, with paid-up capital equal to actual consideration received.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation's Articles of Incorporation filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) are ratified and adopted; RESOLVED, that subscriptions for the initial no-par-value common shares be accepted, and the directors are authorized to allot, issue, and record such shares in the share register; RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at [Registered Office Address], Alberta, and the records address maintained at [Records Address], Alberta; RESOLVED, that [Director Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Director Name] Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, serving at the Board's pleasure; RESOLVED, that the first by-laws be adopted and banking relationships authorized; and RESOLVED, that officers be empowered to execute all statutory filings and licensing applications for the Corporation's operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – NUANS search system (online portal or authorized service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve a distinctive corporate name carrying the mandatory ULC descriptor (e.g., '[Company Name] ULC' or '[Company Name] Unlimited Liability Corporation'). Commission the NUANS Name Search Report, which must be issued no earlier than 90 days before the articles are filed. Verify that the name is not confusingly similar to existing corporate names or registered trademarks, and confirm the report accurately reflects the search on the proposed name and any alternative names.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request and report
Proposed name memorandum with corporate objectives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Corporate Registry refuses the name on distinctiveness or confusion grounds, resubmit with a revised distinctive name and a fresh NUANS report within the 90-day validity window, or file the articles under a numbered name and later apply for a change of name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation for an Unlimited Liability Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – online incorporation filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute the Articles of Incorporation electing to be an unlimited liability corporation under Part 1.1 of the ABCA. Set out the registered office address, the first director(s), and the authorized share structure (typically no-par-value shares with any consents or transfer restrictions needed for ULC tax planning). Attach the NUANS report and the signed consent of each director. Pay the filing fee; upon acceptance the Corporate Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the ULC comes into legal existence.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (executed by the incorporator)
NUANS Name Search Report (valid for 90 days)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries or rejects the filing due to clerical defects, correct the affected schedules and resubmit within 30 days. A formal refusal may be challenged by judicial review at the Court of King's Bench of Alberta; in the interim, the incorporators may incorporate a numbered company to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office, Records Address, and Initial Corporate Registry Returns
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain at all times a physical registered office address in Alberta (a post-office box is prohibited) and appoint a records address where the corporate minute book and share records are kept. Notify the Corporate Registry of any change of registered office or records address and submit the first annual return within the statutory window measured from the anniversary of incorporation, together with current director and officer particulars.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records address particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry flags inconsistencies between the articles, the return, or the address notices, file corrective amendment or notice forms and repay any late-filing penalty; administrative dissolution risks are cured by immediate filing of all arrears and a revival application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Meeting, By-Law Adoption, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the board (or obtain unanimous written resolutions in lieu). Adopt the model by-laws, allot and issue the subscribed common shares, prepare and deliver share certificates, elect officers, appoint the registered office and records custodian, approve the opening of the corporate banking account, and establish the accounting and minute-book framework. All instruments are entered in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural defects in the organizational meeting may be fully remedied by unanimous written resolutions of the directors, retroactive ratification, and a confirmatory meeting; share allotments made without board authority may be ratified by a subsequent directors' resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Jurisdictional Maintenance, Extra-Provincial Registration, and Civil Defense Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; foreign provincial registries (e.g., BC Registry Services) if applicable; municipal fire and OHS authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the ULC carries on business outside Alberta (for example, in British Columbia), register extra-provincially in the other jurisdiction and designate the Alberta registered office as principal office. Establish an annual compliance calendar covering the Corporate Registry annual return, municipal business licence renewal, Alberta OHS workplace clearance, and fire safety certification for the commercial office premises. Keep the amendment and notice filings current for any change in directors, officers, address, or share structure.
required_dossiers: Municipal licence and fire/OHS clearance certificates
Annual compliance calendar and renewal records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If extra-provincial registration is refused or late, apply for a late registration with a certificate of good standing and pay the applicable late fee; revoked municipal licences are reinstated upon demonstration of full code compliance and payment of arrears.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal business licensing authority (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licensing and Community Standards) and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS), Alberta Labour; no provincial industrial permit board applies to advisory-only ISIC 7490 operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Licence (municipal) and OHS workplace registration; no manufacturing, production, or operating permit is triggered by FDA 510(k) and CE Mark regulatory consulting activities, which are office-based professional services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based professional services; no environmental impact assessment registration required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-3, and the Activities Designation Regulation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or stack emission thresholds apply. Sanitary office wastewater is discharged under the municipal sewer-use bylaw; all paper, electronic, and confidential-waste disposal must comply with the Waste Control Regulation (Alta Reg 192/1996) and applicable municipal recycling and e-waste bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for commercial office occupancy under the Alberta Safety Codes Act, SA 2000, c S-1; structural load and building compliance with the Alberta Building Code; Alberta OHS occupational clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 (workplace hazard assessment, emergency response plan, and first-aid requirements); and registration with the Workers' Compensation Board once employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) - federal tax administrator for income tax, GST/HST, payroll and customs program accounts. Portals: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-registration-online.html and the CRA My Business Account portal at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate or register the unlimited liability corporation in Alberta under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (for foreign entities: extra-provincial registration and a registered Alberta address are required; no minimum capital and non-resident ownership are permitted). Step 2 - Obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) online via Business Registration Online, by fax, or by mail; CRA will issue an RT (GST/HST) program account, e.g. 123456789 RT0001, which serves as the tax identifier for GST/HST and income tax. Step 3 - Concurrently add an RM (import/export) program account and, if hiring, an RP (payroll) account. Step 4 - Non-resident directors or shareholders must provide proof of identity, the foreign registration certificate, and the Alberta incorporation certificate; CRA may require a Canadian representative under section 267 Excise Tax Act and may post a security bond under section 308 ETA for non-resident registrants with weak nexus. Step 5 - Registration is effective from the earlier of the date of application and the date of the first taxable supply in Canada. The BN is used across all CRA programs and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) customs reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation for Canadian federal income tax purposes: an Alberta ULC is a corporation and is deemed resident in Canada under subsection 250(4.1) of the Income Tax Act, filing a T2 corporate return and paying Part I tax. Pass_Through_Eligible applies only in cross-border US tax planning: a wholly-owned ULC may be treated as a disregarded entity under US check-the-box rules, a position administratively recognized by CRA in Income Tax Folio S5-F3-C1 for Canada-US treaty application. No territorial-scope regime and no tax-exempt zone status apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no Canadian domestic check-the-box election; hybrid pass-through status is achieved through a US federal Form 8832 classification election combined with CRA administration policy in Income Tax Folio S5-F3-C1. Available Canadian statutory elections: (1) Excise Tax Act section 273 election between closely related corporations to deem taxable supplies to be made for nil consideration, neutralizing intra-group GST; (2) ETA section 238.1 election for affiliated registrants to file a consolidated GST/HST return with CRA approval; (3) ETA section 150 and Part IX elections related to financial services and nil-consideration supplies; (4) Income Tax Act elections relevant to non-resident shareholders of a ULC, including Part XIII withholding treaty claims and subsection 250(5) deeming coordination. No protection against hybrid mismatch adjustment applies for a ULC under Canadian law beyond the OECD BEPS Action 2 rules implemented in Part VI.1 of the Income Tax Act, which may require the entity to be characterized strictly as a corporation unless the US check-the-box election is in force.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) - the federal value-added tax administered by CRA under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. The Province of Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax, no provincial VAT, and no harmonized provincial component; therefore the effective indirect tax rate in CA-AB is the 5% federal GST only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 - the small supplier threshold under subsection 148(1) ETA, measured as worldwide taxable supplies (excluding financial services and supplies of capital property) made by the entity and its associates over the immediately preceding four calendar quarters and the current calendar quarter. Once exceeded, GST/HST registration is mandatory within 29 days after the person ceases to be a small supplier (section 240 ETA). Voluntary registration is permitted for a person making taxable supplies in Canada even below the threshold, enabling input tax credit recovery.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping regime; there is no CRA API clearance or mandatory e-invoice validation for GST/HST purposes. Electronic invoicing is permitted when the supplier's records are legible, reliable and auditable under CRA's Electronic Records Requirements. Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns (GST/HST NETFILE) applies to registrants with annual taxable supplies greater than C$1.5 million; all regime registrants may e-file, and non-resident registrants may be required to appoint a Canadian representative or post security to obtain or maintain registration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: zero-rated under section 1, Part V, Schedule VI ETA when the supplier exports goods in accordance with the Customs Act and retains proof of physical export. Services exports: zero-rated under section 7, Part V, Schedule VI ETA when a registrant supplies a service to a non-resident recipient, provided the service is not (a) in respect of real property situated in Canada, (b) in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, (c) a personal services supply to an individual present in Canada, or (d) a supply to a non-resident GST/HST registrant who acquires the service for consumption, use or enjoyment in Canada. MedTech FDA 510(k) filing and EU CE Mark regulatory consulting deliverables (submission dossiers, regulatory strategy, gap assessments, quality system documentation) are supplied electronically or as reports to non-resident medical device manufacturers, and therefore qualify for 0% GST, provided the client is a non-resident person not acquiring the advisory service for Canadian business use. Where the client is a Canadian-resident GST/HST registrant, the supply is taxable at 5% with input tax credit offset. The supplier must maintain a complete export service file: signed contract with the non-resident client, evidence of the client's non-resident status, proof of electronic or courier delivery of deliverables outside Canada, and foreign-source payment records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A/E14 CUS) - required only where any tangible goods are physically exported from Canada
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill - proof of physical export for any goods component of the transaction
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign bank transfer record - evidence of settlement from a non-resident bank account
Signed consulting services agreement with the non-resident client stating the FDA 510(k) / EU CE Mark regulatory scope and electronic delivery method
W-8BEN-E or equivalent certification of non-residence obtained from the client for treaty and documentation purposes

Detailed statement of work and invoice describing the offshore regulatory advisory deliverables and confirming no Canadian real property, Canadian-situated goods, or personal services in Canada are involved
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated export claims for 4 years from the date of the notice of assessment under section 298 ETA, extended to 7 years where a claim involves negligence, carelessness, wilful default, misrepresentation, or a failure to file. Export zero-rating is audited where the supplier cannot substantiate the non-resident recipient, the offshore delivery, or the foreign payment; on reversal, the supplier owes 5% GST on the full consideration plus statutory interest and principal. Penalty regime: subsection 285(1) ETA gross-negligence penalty of the greater of C$250 and 25% of the net-tax understatement or refund overstatement; subsection 280(1) ETA penalty of 25% of any tax or refund knowingly or recklessly obtained that should not have been claimed; criminal prosecution for wilful evasion under sections 327-328 ETA with fines up to C$25,000 (summary) or unlimited fines and up to 5 years imprisonment (indictable). Directors are jointly and severally liable for the ULC's unremitted or incorrectly refunded GST/HST under section 323 ETA. Canada imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for GST/HST zero-rating; the 180-day benchmark is a prudent internal compliance convention, and prolonged non-repatriation of export proceeds may trigger a CRA commercial-reality review of whether a genuine export supply occurred. For the ULC structure specifically, the unlimited liability feature exposes each shareholder's assets directly to any CRA clawback assessment, penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free convertibility regime for both capital and current account transactions under the Foreign Exchange Act. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted, subject solely to standard corporate filings, tax reporting, and beneficial ownership disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canadian exporters must report export transactions to Statistics Canada within 30 days of shipment. No mandatory surrender or conversion ratio applies; foreign exchange conversion remains at the exporter's discretion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business) are feasible for limited cross-border transfers but require FINTRAC registration, corporate KYC verification, and may not support full liquidity clearing or hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and video interviews are permitted for directors and officers under FINTRAC guidelines; physical presence is not mandatory for standard corporate account opening but may be requested for enhanced due diligence or high-value transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate register extracts, director/officer identification, and source-of-wealth documentation
Transaction purpose letters, independent verification reports, and beneficial ownership certificates

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires use SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes 'EQTY' for equity contributions or 'LOAN' for loans. Verification requires corporate charter, director resolutions, and beneficial ownership certificates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements via SWIFT MT103 or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banking networks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 (approx. USD 75) if filed after 60-day window; failure to file for three consecutive years may trigger administrative dissolution by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An auditor must be appointed unless all shareholders unanimously waive appointment (ABCA s.158); distributing (public) corporations are subject to mandatory audit, but non-distributing private ULCs may pass a unanimous resolution to exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS required for publicly accountable enterprises; otherwise ASPE permitted, with an option to adopt IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under ABCA s.114.1, a register of individuals with significant control (ISC) must be maintained and updated within 15 days of any share transfer or issuance; no annual government filing is required, but an annual internal confirmation must be obtained from each ISC holder to verify the continued accuracy of their recorded information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% general corporate rate; 9% small business rate for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations with taxable capital under $500,000; R&D tax credit (up to 15% of qualified expenditures); investment tax credits for eligible manufacturing or processing; no broad-based tax holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporate Income Tax Return filed electronically through CRA My Business Account portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 fiscal year-end requires filing by June 30)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate revenue from all sources including consulting fees for FDA 510(k) and CE Mark regulatory compliance services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for resident corporations; non-residents report worldwide income if carrying on business in Canada

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after allowable deductions including salaries, office expenses, and professional fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents file T2 with additional schedules for Canadian-source income and may face branch tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions, losses, and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may have withholding tax on certain payments and must report Canadian-source income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated corporate tax liability after applicable credits and surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents subject to branch tax on after-tax earnings remitted to head office

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $50 per day to a maximum of $5,000; interest charges at 1% per month on unpaid taxes; potential criminal prosecution for willful evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholders must submit Treaty Relief Certificate application (Form NR301) to CRA with supporting documentation including ownership proof and beneficial ownership details; approval required prior to dividend remittance; process typically takes 30-60 days
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0% under US-Canada tax treaty; Royalties: 10% statutory rate, reduced to 0-6.6% under most treaties including US

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in related-party transactions for local file; CAD 50,000,000 in gross revenue for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada lacks a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations regime similar to EU; compliance assessed under General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and transfer pricing provisions requiring commercial and economic substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to report taxable income or claiming false deductions on T2 return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $100,000 per count or imprisonment for up to 2 years; director liability for unpaid taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors personally liable for corporate tax debts; possible criminal charges and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining ULC without real business operations or decision-making in Alberta
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR adjustments recharacterizing income; penalties of 10-50% of tax benefit; potential dissolution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil penalties, restitution orders; in severe cases, travel bans or director disqualifications

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct proper due diligence on beneficial owners or report suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $10,000,000; license revocation for regulated activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment for willful non-compliance; director disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation or apply arm's length principle to intercompany transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 10% to 50% of transfer pricing adjustments; interest on underpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for tax underpayments; potential criminal liability in egregious cases
